current.text: Reports say he is likely to start at center for New Orleans over Derik Queen. The other likely starters are Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy and Dejounte Murray.
New Orleans has a crowded frontcourt with Zion Williamson and Derik Queen. Experts think Queen and Zion do not fit together, which helps Missi's case to start.
Experts expect a bigger role for him under new coach Jamahl Mosley.
Josh sees him as a worthwhile late flier around pick 120. As a starter he offers two-block upside, high FG% and double-digit rebounds, and he is available everywhere.
Mosley's defense switches less than the old scheme. Jake thinks that could help his weak defensive rebounding.

durable.text: He is a strong rim protector. He contests shots at the rim at a high rate, and he turned 39% of his rim contests into blocks last season.
Blocks are his standout category. They are far above the top 250 pool.
He is a poor defensive rebounder for a center, around the bottom 10% at his position.
He makes no threes and gets very few steals. Both are weak even for a center.
His FT% is low, but he takes only about 2 free throws a game, so the damage is limited.

note: He sits right at our 144-player cutoff (Yahoo rank 143, ESPN 164, 0 USD value on both sites, and 2 USD in our auction last season), so he is a 1 to 2 USD end-of-draft pick for blocks. He fits punt 3PM and punt STL builds best, and he adds FG% on low volume and few turnovers. Early in the season, check that he starts over Derik Queen and plays clearly more than last season's 19.6 minutes. If he does not, he goes back to waivers.
